title: Model deployment options and configuration parameters
learningObjective: Identify appropriate deployment types (Global, Data Zone, Standard, Provisioned, Batch) and deployment and request parameters for a model in Microsoft Foundry.
foundation: Before you can call a model in Foundry, you deploy it: you give it a deployment name, choose a deployment type, and set limits.
The deployment type decides where requests are processed and how you pay: pay per token (Standard types), reserved capacity (Provisioned), or cheap delayed processing (Batch).
Parameters come in two kinds: deployment settings (name, version, rate limit, content filter) chosen once, and request parameters (temperature, top_p, max output tokens) sent with each call.
engineer: Global Standard: pay per token; requests may be processed in any Azure region with capacity; highest default quota; the usual starting point. Data at rest stays in your resource's geography.
Data Zone Standard: pay per token; processing stays within a data zone (EU or US). Standard (regional): processing within the resource's region/geography.

Provisioned (Global, Data Zone, Regional): reserve provisioned throughput units (PTU) for predictable latency and throughput; billed hourly for capacity (with reservations available), whether or not you use it.

Batch (Global, Data Zone): submit large files of requests asynchronously; target turnaround 24 hours; about 50% lower cost than Global Standard; separate quota. Developer deployments are for evaluating fine-tuned models.

Deployment settings: model and version, version upgrade policy (auto-update to default, or pin), deployment name (what code passes as model=), tokens-per-minute rate limit (from regional quota; also sets requests per minute), content filter configuration, and dynamic quota options.
Request parameters: temperature, top_p, max_output_tokens, stop sequences, response format (structured output), tools; reasoning models may use reasoning effort instead of temperature.

example.title: Three deployments, one model
body: A European bank deploys the same chat model three times: Data Zone Standard (EU) for its customer assistant, Data Zone Provisioned for its high-volume call-centre copilot that needs steady latency, and Global Batch for nightly classification of non-personal research documents.
Each has a clear deployment name, a pinned model version and the strictest content filter for the customer-facing app.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User on the Foundry project to use models and agents; Azure AI Project Manager or Owner to create projects and deployments
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Foundry portal > Models + endpoints > Deploy model: choose deployment type, name, version upgrade policy, TPM, content filter.
Management center > Quota: see TPM quota per region and model.
configuration.cli:
# Create a Foundry resource and project (billable only when used)
az group create --name rg-ai901 --location eastus2
az cognitiveservices account create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --location eastus2 --custom-domain contoso-ai --allow-project-management
az cognitiveservices account project create --name support --resource-group rg-ai901 --account-name contoso-ai
# Deploy a model (Global Standard, 50K TPM)
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --deployment-name chat-model --model-name gpt-5-mini --model-version <version> --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 50
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-ai901 -Location eastus2
New-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai -Type AIServices -SkuName S0 -Location eastus2 -CustomSubdomainName contoso-ai
# Projects and deployments: use the Foundry portal or Azure CLI
configuration.python:
response = openai.responses.create(
    model="chat-model",
    input="Suggest three names for a cat cafe.",
    temperature=1.0,        # more creative
    max_output_tokens=100,  # cap the answer length
)
print(response.output_text, response.usage.input_tokens, response.usage.output_tokens)

Passing the model family name instead of the deployment name
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.fix: Retry with backoff, raise TPM within quota, or use Provisioned.

comparisons.difference: Standard is pay-per-token with shared capacity; Provisioned reserves throughput for predictable performance.
Global may process anywhere; Data Zone keeps processing in the EU or US.

misconceptions.myth: Global deployments store your data anywhere.
misconceptions.reality: Data at rest stays in your geography; only processing may be global.

misconceptions.myth: model= is the model family name.

architectureDecisions: Start with Global Standard unless residency rules apply.
Use Provisioned for steady, high, latency-sensitive load.
Use Batch for large offline jobs.
